title: Short Stuff: Look-Alike Old Couples
summary: Short Stuff episode on why old couples start to look alike. The hosts describe a study in which people matched married couples' photos better than chance, with pairs rated similarly for attractiveness, and discuss genetic similarity, shared personality and expressions, and shared life experiences as possible explanations. They then cover genetic compatibility in mate selection, sexual imprinting (women seeking partners resembling close fathers, including in adoptive cases), symmetry and attractiveness, waist-to-hip ratio, and finally the tendency of people to look like their dogs, including a 2004 study on people choosing purebred dogs that resemble them.
topics: pet owners look like their dogs

segments.title: Opening banter and why couples look alike
segments.summary: The hosts joke about looking alike after their anniversary, define older couples, and ask why long-term partners come to resemble each other.

segments.title: Study on matching married couples by photo
segments.summary: A study had participants (eleven men and eleven women) match photos of married couples. People paired couples above chance, and rated attractiveness similarly within pairs. The hosts attribute the resemblance mostly to genetics, with shared personality and expressions as other factors.
topics: shared expressions and personality in couples

segments.title: Genetic similarity and mate selection
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the idea that people seek partners who are genetically similar but not too similar, and ask how someone could judge genetic compatibility.

segments.title: Sexual imprinting on fathers
segments.summary: Studies suggest women tend to seek partners resembling fathers they were close to, with the effect stronger with stronger bonds. The same pattern was reported for adoptive daughters, who imprint on their genetic fathers, which the hosts note complicates the genetic argument.

segments.title: Symmetry, waist-to-hip ratio and attractiveness
segments.summary: Facial and body symmetry are described as universal markers of beauty linked to health. Men are said to prefer a waist-to-hip ratio of about 0.7 in women, and the hosts explain fat distribution is driven by hormones. Symmetry is also linked in studies to more sexual partners.

segments.title: Couples dressing alike and dogs that look like owners
segments.summary: The hosts note couples sometimes dress alike, then turn to people looking like their dogs. A 2004 study reportedly found people who buy purebred dogs tend to choose dogs that resemble them.
topics: pet owners look like their dogs

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts wrap up the episode and close with the show's credits.
